spec.description: CWN Network Operations — abstracted AP telemetry. v12 brings AP2 (192.168.1.101, mesh-connected over 802.11s on phy1-mesh0) fully online: 'Node status', 'AP Resource Health', and the station health table are now genuinely parametrized by $ap (job="openwrt-$ap-node"/"openwrt-$ap-wifi"), which the v10/v11 description had already announced but the dashboard did not yet implement. Two fixed 'AP1/AP2 status' panels are added alongside the $ap-driven ones so node availability is visible without using the dropdown. New 'Mesh Backhaul' row exposes SNR, signal, and packet-loss on the AP1↔AP2 802.11s link (phy1-mesh0), reported from AP1's side as the canonical, non-duplicated view of the (symmetric) link. v12.1 patch: added job="openwrt-ap1-qdisc" filter to the Network Health Check WiFi-side term and job="openwrt-ap1-mesh-qdisc" filter to the new Mesh Backhaul packet-loss panel, closing a label-collision gap that would have silently summed AP1 and AP2s qdisc series together once AP2s own qdisc exporter went live. v12.1: connected-clients count now sums AP1+AP2 (was AP1-only); added per-node 'Issues — AP1'/'Issues — AP2' triage panels to Operator Actions Needed, counting CPU, memory, link-flap, and qdisc-loss threshold breaches per node. v12.2: 'Issues — AP1'/'Issues — AP2' replaced with a single 'Network Issue Summary' panel switching between three message states via a 25-way composite value mapping. Mesh SNR and Mesh RSSI panels now show a Weak/Fair/Good-style verdict with plain-language narration instead of the raw dB/dBm number, matching the rest of the dashboard's house style (Signal quality, Link stability, etc).

spec.title: Station health table — $ap (phy0-ap0)
spec.description: Per-station WiFi health table for the node selected in the AP Node dropdown above.

spec.title: Top Applications by Data Volume (24 hrs)
spec.description: Top applications by data volume, addressing the survey finding that 3/3 operators want per-application data usage visibility, and reflecting the heavy-hitter traffic concentration observed in the CN measurement study (up to 86.8% of volume from 4 applications).

spec.title: Total Data Consumption (24hrs)
spec.description: Total data consumption (network accounting) alongside how it compares to your expected daily baseline ($avg_daily_consumption_gb, editable dashboard variable). Percentage verdict: green <50%, orange 50-75%, red >=75% of that baseline.

spec.title: Gateway Bandwidth Saturation (Upload / Download)
spec.description: Internet uplink (WAN) saturation, shown separately for upload and download since this backhaul is asymmetric ($wan_capacity_mbps_up / $wan_capacity_mbps_down, editable dashboard variables). A single combined figure would misrepresent whichever direction has the smaller capacity. Detects the shared, network-wide bottleneck operators specifically flagged in the survey ('no way to know if network has reached capacity') — distinct from radio congestion. High usage here with a clear WiFi Channel verdict points to too many concurrent heavy users or heavy-hitter apps (cf. traffic structure findings) saturating the actual Internet connection, not the local radio.

spec.title: AP Resource Health — CPU & Memory ($ap)
spec.description: AP router CPU and memory, each against its own literature-grounded threshold. CPU: 70%/90% (Harchol-Balter; PASTRAMI 2024; Agarwal et al.) -- sustained high CPU on a single-core MIPS AP indicates overload. Memory: 80%/90%, following the Nagios check_mem convention (warning below 20% free, critical below 10% free).

spec.title: Connection Speed (QoE)
spec.description: QoE verdict driven by P90 (tail) latency rather than average RTT, per the CN measurement study finding that tail-latency variability drives user-perceived performance more than mean delay. Thresholds are informed by the baseline-vs-effective RTT divergence observed in the Malawi and South Africa CN traces (indicative — tune per deployment).

0.text: Degraded — connection is slow, check for heavy use or contact your provider

1.text: Elevated — some users may notice delays

spec.title: Name Resolution (DNS Health)
spec.description: DNS health verdict from the ratio of failed responses (NXDOMAIN/NOTIMP) to total queries. Grounded in the CN measurement study's finding that DNS failures are heavily concentrated among a small number of destinations — a rising failure ratio points to resolver misconfiguration, upstream reliability issues, or possible DGA/malicious traffic.

spec.title: Connected clients (AP1 + AP2)
spec.description: Total stations associated across both nodes' client-facing radios. v12.1: previously only counted AP1.

spec.title: Packet Loss
spec.description: Packet loss ratio measured on active QoE probes (iperf/ping-derived) between the gateway and Internet. Elevated loss degrades real-time applications (VoIP, video calls) disproportionately, per operator-reported frustration with 'packet loss' as a regular issue.

spec.title: Jitter
spec.description: Inter-packet delay variation on active QoE probes. High jitter degrades VoIP/video call quality even when average latency and loss remain acceptable.

spec.title: DHCP Pool Available
spec.description: Share of the DHCP address pool still available for new clients, from the DHCP lease exporter. Low availability means new devices cannot obtain an IP address — the DHCP allocation failure condition named directly by the Colnodo operator.

spec.title: DHCP Health
spec.description: DHCP health verdict from remaining pool capacity. A pool nearing exhaustion means the next client to associate will fail to obtain an address — expand the pool or investigate stale leases before this reaches zero.

0.text: Pool exhausted — clients failing to obtain IP, expand pool

spec.title: Link flaps (15m)-($ap)
spec.description: AP interface link flap events in the last hour. 0 = stable.

spec.title: Network Health Check($ap)
spec.description: Combined connectivity verdict, triangulating loss measured at two different points: the gateway's active QoE probe to the Internet (WAN-side, via latency.py's fping-based packet loss and jitter computation), and drop-to-attempted-packet ratio on AP1's station-facing radio, phy0-ap0 (local Wi-Fi-side, from node_exporter's built-in netdev collector). Both halves use an 'or vector(0)' fallback so a missing/undefined metric on either side, e.g. a transient fping failure or a temporary AP1 scrape gap, defaults to 'no issue detected' on that side rather than blanking the whole panel (PromQL returns an empty result, not zero, when summing over zero series, and empty-plus-anything is also empty). This fallback is intentional, permanent resilience, not a workaround for missing functionality: node_qoe_packet_loss_ratio and node_qoe_jitter_ms are implemented in latency.py as of Aug 2026, so all four verdict states (0-3) are expected to be reachable once that script is deployed and confirmed via manual test run. WAN threshold (1%) matches the existing Connection Reliability panel's 'monitor' boundary; the local Wi-Fi threshold (1% of attempted TX+RX packets on phy0-ap0) is a new, interpretable default with no directly applicable prior threshold literature, a candidate for future empirical tuning. Scoped to the wireless hop to stations; does not cover AP1's own Ethernet uplink to the gateway, a distinct third failure domain noted as a direction for future extension. [v12.1: WiFi-side term now filtered to job="openwrt-ap1-qdisc" to prevent collision with AP2s identical device="phy0-ap0" series once AP2s own qdisc exporter comes online.]

spec.expr: sum((node_qoe_packet_loss_ratio{job="gw-latency"} * 100 > bool 1) or vector(0)) * 2 + sum((100 * rate(node_wifi_qdisc_dropped_packets_total{job="openwrt-$ap-qdisc", device="phy0-ap0"}[5m]) / clamp_min(rate(node_wifi_qdisc_sent_packets_total{job="openwrt-$ap-qdisc", device="phy0-ap0"}[5m]) + rate(node_wifi_qdisc_dropped_packets_total{job="openwrt-$ap-qdisc", device="phy0-ap0"}[5m]), 1) > bool 1) or vector(0))

1.text: Wi-Fi issue — check signal, interference, or channel congestion

2.text: Internet issue — check WAN link or contact your provider

3.text: Multiple issues — check both Wi-Fi and Internet connection

spec.title: Gateway Packet Loss
spec.description: Packet loss ratio measured on active QoE probes (iperf/ping-derived) between the gateway and Internet. Elevated loss degrades real-time applications (VoIP, video calls) disproportionately, per operator-reported frustration with 'packet loss' as a regular issue.

spec.title: WiFi Channel Saturation
spec.description: Radio medium (airtime) saturation, from channel-busy-time ratio via 'iw survey dump' on the AP itself. Detects contention/interference/retransmission load independent of backhaul usage — e.g. many weak-signal clients can saturate airtime even when the Internet uplink is nearly idle. High airtime use with low Gateway Bandwidth usage points to channel congestion, not an Internet-capacity problem — consider changing channel, reducing channel width, or adding an AP.

spec.title: AP1 status
spec.description: Fixed reachability check for ap1, shown independently of the AP Node dropdown so both nodes' availability is visible at a glance without switching.

spec.title: AP2 status
spec.description: Fixed reachability check for ap2, shown independently of the AP Node dropdown so both nodes' availability is visible at a glance without switching.

spec.title: Mesh link SNR (AP1 ↔ AP2)
spec.description: Verdict derived from raw mesh SNR on phy1-mesh0 (AP1's side, canonical). 0-12.4dB=Weak, 12.5-24.9dB=Fair, >=25dB=Good.

1.text: Fair — monitor, may need attention soon

spec.title: Mesh link signal (AP1 ↔ AP2)
spec.description: Verdict derived from raw mesh RSSI on phy1-mesh0 (AP1's side, canonical). <=-90dBm=Weak, -89 to -71dBm=Moderate, >=-70dBm=Strong.

1.text: Moderate — usable, keep an eye on it

spec.title: Mesh link packet loss (AP1 ↔ AP2)
spec.description: Drop-to-attempted-packet ratio on the mesh backhaul interface phy1-mesh0, using the same qdisc-based formula as the existing Network Health Check's Wi-Fi-side term, retargeted from phy0-ap0 to phy1-mesh0. If AP2 loses backhaul, clients still associated to AP2 lose Internet access even though AP2 itself may still show 'Online.' [v12.1: now reads from the dedicated wifi_qdisc_health_mesh.sh / job="openwrt-ap1-mesh-qdisc" scrape target, not the AP-facing qdisc job.]

spec.title: Network Issue Summary
spec.description: Single-panel rollup replacing the separate AP1/AP2 issue counters. Encodes (AP1 issue count * 10 + AP2 issue count) as a composite code, 00-44, mapped to one of three message patterns: no issues, issues on one AP only (named), or issues on both (combined total). Same four underlying checks per node as before: CPU >85%, memory >85%, >3 link flaps/5m, qdisc packet loss >5%.

spec.expr: (sum((1 - rate(node_cpu_seconds_total{job="openwrt-ap1-node", mode="idle"}[5m])) * 100 > bool 85 or vector(0)) + sum((1 - node_memory_MemAvailable_bytes{job="openwrt-ap1-node"} / node_memory_MemTotal_bytes{job="openwrt-ap1-node"}) * 100 > bool 85 or vector(0)) + sum(floor(increase(node_network_carrier_changes_total{job="openwrt-ap1-node", device="phy0-ap0"}[5m])) > bool 3 or vector(0)) + sum(100 * rate(node_wifi_qdisc_dropped_packets_total{job="openwrt-ap1-qdisc", device="phy0-ap0"}[5m]) / clamp_min(rate(node_wifi_qdisc_sent_packets_total{job="openwrt-ap1-qdisc", device="phy0-ap0"}[5m]) + rate(node_wifi_qdisc_dropped_packets_total{job="openwrt-ap1-qdisc", device="phy0-ap0"}[5m]), 1) > bool 5 or vector(0))) * 10 + (sum((1 - rate(node_cpu_seconds_total{job="openwrt-ap2-node", mode="idle"}[5m])) * 100 > bool 85 or vector(0)) + sum((1 - node_memory_MemAvailable_bytes{job="openwrt-ap2-node"} / node_memory_MemTotal_bytes{job="openwrt-ap2-node"}) * 100 > bool 85 or vector(0)) + sum(floor(increase(node_network_carrier_changes_total{job="openwrt-ap2-node", device="phy0-ap0"}[5m])) > bool 3 or vector(0)) + sum(100 * rate(node_wifi_qdisc_dropped_packets_total{job="openwrt-ap2-qdisc", device="phy0-ap0"}[5m]) / clamp_min(rate(node_wifi_qdisc_sent_packets_total{job="openwrt-ap2-qdisc", device="phy0-ap0"}[5m]) + rate(node_wifi_qdisc_dropped_packets_total{job="openwrt-ap2-qdisc", device="phy0-ap0"}[5m]), 1) > bool 5 or vector(0)))

spec.title: Link stability-($ap)
spec.description: Link stability verdict from carrier change events over 7 days. Persistent flapping needs physical investigation.

spec.title: Memory pressure ($ap)
spec.description: Memory pressure verdict, re-aligned to match the AP Resource Health panel's Nagios check_mem convention: below 80% used is healthy, 80-90% used is a warning, 90%+ used is critical (equivalently: below 20% available is a warning, below 10% available is critical). Previously used a separate, uncoordinated 20%-step convention (orange at 60% used) that disagreed with the redesigned combined panel measuring the same underlying metric.

spec.label: WAN Upload Capacity (Mbps)
spec.description: Known Internet uplink capacity in Mbps (upload direction). Set to your actual backhaul plan speed. Split from download capacity because this backhaul is asymmetric.

spec.name: wan_capacity_mbps_down
